sources.title: Pine sample transfer: eligibility conditions (v1)
sources.body: Work for Pine sample transfer in the south area may proceed if and only if its area policy is adopted and remaining coolant hours is at least 5. These are the complete operational eligibility conditions. A withdrawn or proposed policy blocks work regardless of the measurement. The threshold uses the current measurement log, not the planning estimate. Handoff recordkeeping is a separate obligation, not an additional eligibility prerequisite.

sources.title: Pine sample transfer: handoff instructions (v1)
sources.body:
For Pine sample transfer in the south area, Tala 16 is the transfer custodian. The next operator must receive the custody manifest. Retain this handoff record for 45 days. A signed receipt proves delivery but does not replace the named handoff item. This handoff rule is independent of policy revisions and remains in force after a withdrawal.

The receiving operator checks the item title, the covered area, and the source revision before accepting custody. If an earlier operator supplied a different limit, the receiving operator records the discrepancy and consults the active area policy. A handoff may be stored while operations are blocked; storing it does not authorize the underlying work. Missing information remains unknown until a source provides it.

Record classification: an inspection log documents a check; a dispatch list documents intended movements; a receipt register documents receipt; an incident note documents an exception. These records have separate purposes. Do not rename one record to satisfy the requirement for another. For unrelated annex areas, consult their companion records in the area table.
